text:
incident-bot: ALERT: prefill-gpu OOM detected on prefill-prod-3 at 2026-03-17T02:15:09Z. Container restart + SIGSEGV observed. Auto-bridged to #incidents. Trace id: trace-82a5
alex: I'm on it. seeing repeated OOMs when handling long prompts (>1.2M tokens in window)
maria: stack traces look like a device-side assert then container restart. suspect KV cache blowup during prefill.
sam: copying tail logs from container: 
```
[2026-03-17T02:14:52Z] PREFILL: incoming request id=req-9bba size=1.4M tokens
[2026-03-17T02:15:03Z] CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY at runtime/attention.cu: line 412
[2026-03-17T02:15:04Z] Segmentation fault (signal 11)
[2026-03-17T02:15:05Z] container restart by kubelet, exit code 137
```
jess: Support: two customer incidents flagged — AcmeDocs and LongChatCorp both saw degraded responses/connection resets in last 5m. Notified via status page.
leo: Product: both customers were using large-context beta. We should give them ETA ASAP and recommend fallback to 256k window in their SDKs.
katelyn: Ops: which mitigation do we want first — node cordon+drain, runtime rollback, or temporary prefill input size clamp?
alex: priority: prevent further restarts. Quick mitigation = cluster-level prefilling throttle + runtime mem-safety flag. I'll push a temporary kill switch to drop prefill if >512k tokens.
maria: Agree. Also disable aggressive KV prefetch for the runtime on prefill-prod-3 (patching config: `runtime.prefetch.kv=false`). Will patch now.
ops-bot: Applying config change to prefill-prod-3: patch runtime.prefetch.kv=false (rolling update)
sam: adding a short-lived guard in the router: `if prefill_length > 524288 -> route to coldmodel` and set `X-Redwood-Reason: pref_limit`
jess: Notifying customers: message ready? I can update AcmeDocs with recommended workaround and that we're applying throttles.
leo: Draft: "We're seeing GPU memory crashes on very large prefills. We've applied throttles and a temporary routing change to reduce large-prefill traffic. No data lost, but responses may load slower. We expect normal service in ~30-60m while we stabilize"
jess: sending now to both customers. pinging for confirmation.
alex: config patch complete. watch CPU/GPU metrics.
maria: I see OOM count dropping on prefill-prod-3 but there are still 2 container restarts in the last 3 mins. Rolling restart in progress for updated runtime with safer allocation path (image: runtime:v1.2.4-safealloc).
sam: runtime rollout started: `kubectl set image deploy/prefill-runtime prefill-runtime=redwood/runtime:v1.2.4-safealloc -n inference-prefill`
ops-bot: Rollout status: 5/5 updated, 2 pods restarted, all pods healthy.
alex: Good. Observability: token drop rate down 85%, request success back to 98% for prefills under 512k.
maria: I'm pulling a heap profile from crashed container for postmortem: `gcore` not available, grabbing /proc/pid/maps and dmesg.
leo: Customer update queued: I'll mention the runtime patch and suggest clients cap prefill to 512k until we finish the kvcache redesign.
jess: AcmeDocs responded: "Thanks. Can you guarantee no restarts?" I replied: "We're seeing immediate improvement; full fix requires model runtime change, ETA 2-3 days, we'll continue to route large prefills to coldmodel."
katelyn: On-call rotation: alex will continue incident lead for next 45m, maria will handle postmortem artifacts, sam will validate kernel/driver traces.
alex: Confirming - I'll keep a bridge open and escalate to infra if restarts resume.
maria: Early hypothesis for postmortem: unbounded KV prefetch + large context -> transient device allocation exceeding fragmentation threshold -> device-side assert -> segfault. We need allocation guard + fragmentation mitigation.
sam: Also file bug with GPU vendor for `device-side assert` reproducible trace attached.
ops-bot: Incident note created: incident-20260317-prefill-oom-segfault. Assigned tags: prefill, gpu-oom, segfault, customer-impact.
jess: Customer-facing status updated. No billing/consistency impact reported.
leo: Product follow-up: schedule model / runtime test harness for long-context fuzzer (1.5M window) and add to pre-prod gate.
alex: Closing tasks for live mitigation: throttles applied, runtime patched, customers notified. We'll keep monitoring for 2 hours. If everything stable by +2h, we'll resolve the incident.
maria: I'll start the postmortem doc and include timeline + heap snapshots.
alex: thanks all. :thumbsup:
